text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper and aluminium prices are likely to opt for consolidation during early Wednesday trading, as markets mark time ahead of August traded option declarations soon after 1000 gmt, traders said.
Copper should be comfortable above $2,270, while aluminium's downside defence is pegged at $1,700/1,710, they said.

Slow conditions this week suggest that there is little real incentive for the market to break significantly in either direction, as speculative interest and fund involvement in now being directed elsewhere in the complex, traders said.
LME trader Brandeis said that the market is rangebound between support at $2,270 and resistance at $2,305/10, but does look oversold now with the RSI having fallen to 41.5 percent.
However, the market is under downside pressure and really needs to close above $2,320 to relieve this, analyst Harry Creates of Amalgamated Metal Trading noted.
"On the downside $2,270 is important support and if broken falls to $2,235 could be seen," he said.
At 0754 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,295/98, down some $12 from Tuesday's late close.
Tuesday morning's action, when prices fell from near $1,750 to $1,712, was not unexpected, as the market had been sending out overbought signals, traders said.
There is likely to be further consolidation now above the $1,700 level, Brandeis said.
Amalgamated's Creates agreed that the market was consolidating between support and resistance at $1,710 and $1,749 respectively.
At 0754 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,725/28, unchanged from the overnight close.
